rationale: Structure has all 9 sections with clear markdown. Faithfulness fails due to fabricated quotes ('Changing the audience...', 'The most common feedback...'), unsupported title, 'Harrison Chase' surname, onboarding claim, and branch/commit detail not in source. Coverage omits 13.5k stars, 900+ forks, 20k npm downloads, flowchart diagram, and MIT license. Precision weak: 36-38% vague range, invented quotes. Compression suffers from repeated 'Why this section matters' boilerplate and overlapping summaries.
hallucinations: The project's genesis came from a question by LangChain's CEO, Harrison Chase.
User feedback quickly revealed that humans also found the wiki useful for onboarding to new codebases.
"Changing the audience changes what good looks like."
"The most common feedback after launch came from humans using the wiki to onboard onto unfamiliar repos. So it has two audiences now."
The CLI creates a new branch, commits the changes, and opens a pull request for a human to review and merge.
